observations.behavior: Adds pagination, page-cap enforcement, and tiered lookback for MailerSend activity ingestion.
observations.posthog_connection: Checks MailerSend's page 1000 cap and stops pagination to avoid 422 errors.

observations.behavior: Replaces generic paginator with MailerSendPaginator, which respects the page cap.
observations.posthog_connection: Uses MailerSendPaginator instead of JSONResponsePaginator to enforce page cap.

observations.behavior: Adds tiered lookback configuration and fallback tier narrowing on 422.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows account-specific retention tiers; fallback tier narrowing is not shown in this chunk.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains only test additions and assertions. No implementation, configuration, or shared utility changes are supplied. The tier-clamping and page-cap behavior described in comments and assertions cannot be verified against actual production behavior.

observations.behavior: Adds a test asserting that when a database incremental field value is older than the tier's lookback window, the window is clamped to the tier's lookback duration.
observations.posthog_connection: This could support MailerSend warehouse ingestion, where account tier limits the retained history; the implementation of this clamp is not shown, so the benefit is unverified.

observations.behavior: Adds a parameterized test asserting that pagination stops when the next page exceeds the documented page cap, rather than following a link that returns an error.
observations.code_quote: assert [r["id"] for r in rows] == expected_ids
observations.posthog_connection: This could support MailerSend warehouse ingestion, where the API advertises a next link for page 1001 but rejects it; the implementation of the page-cap stop is not shown, so the benefit is unverified.

observations.behavior: Adds a test asserting that when an account's activity retention is exceeded, the window is narrowed to the next tier rather than failing the whole sync.
observations.posthog_connection: This could support MailerSend warehouse ingestion, where account tier limits the retained history; the implementation of this tier-step-down is not shown, so the benefit is unverified.
